sortRows() early-returns when fewer than 2 StandardRows are present (intentional optimisation). This means a grid with exactly 1 row never exercises the usort path — unit tests with 2+ rows are needed to verify sort correctness in CI.

getSortCallback() null guard is correct (checked before usort call in Callback mode), but getSortMode() returning Callback with a null callback is a degenerate state not caught at column configuration time. A defensive check or validation in the column API would prevent silent no-ops.

comments.note: getSortURL() derives the path portion from parse_url($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']). REQUEST_URI is attacker-controlled input. The returned string is a raw URL — callers must HTML-encode it before embedding in HTML attributes. The project's HTMLTag convention (used by all renderer output paths) handles this correctly, so there is no live vulnerability, but a @return docblock note advising callers to HTML-encode would improve safety at future call sites.

setColumnParam() and setDirectionParam() are silently ignored if called after any getSortColumn() or getSortDir() invocation, because resolveSortState() sets $resolved = true on first access. This mirrors the limitation of ArrayPagination's URL parameters but is not documented. Adding a runtime warning or a @throws annotation when params are changed post-resolution would improve DX.

compareValues() correctly handles numeric vs string types. Mixed-type comparisons (one numeric, one non-numeric) fall through to the strcasecmp((string)$a, ...) path rather than numeric comparison — this is a defensible choice but differs from how JavaScript comparators handle mixed types. Worth documenting the intended sentinel for edge cases in a future test.
